en.commentary:
Continuous glucose monitoring became a mainstream wellness tool in 2026, and this ranking reflects that shift. My top pick is Dexcom Stelo because it solves the single biggest barrier to entry: cost and access. You get a G7-grade sensor for 15 days at $49.50, no prescription, no membership, no coaching upsell you never asked for. For most people curious about how a bowl of rice or a morning run moves their glucose, that is exactly the right amount of hardware.

Abbott Lingo lands at number two on the strength of its app. The biosensor accuracy sits around a 9% MARD, close enough to Stelo for wellness use, and the coaching layer that scores your food, sleep and exercise is the most beginner-friendly experience I have tested. If you want the data to arrive with a plan, Lingo earns the premium.

The medical-grade tier still belongs to the Dexcom G7 and the FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus. The G7's 8% MARD and 30-minute warmup remain the accuracy benchmark, and its insulin-pump integration is why insulin users should look here first. The Libre 3 Plus answers with a 15-day sensor, an 8.2% MARD and the smallest footprint on the market, which makes it the value champion for daily diabetes management.

The software platforms, Levels, Nutrisense and Signos, are where the money gets serious. Levels has the cleanest interface, Nutrisense includes a real dietitian in every plan, and Signos owns the weight-loss and GLP-1 use case with FDA-cleared claims. They cost several times what a bare sensor does, and that premium buys interpretation and coaching, since these platforms run the same sensors you can buy alone. I recommend them when you genuinely want guidance. Ultrahuman M1 and Sibionics GS3 round out the biohacker and budget ends, and January AI earns a spot for predicting glucose response with no sensor at all.

highlights.title: Dexcom Stelo is the right first CGM for almost everyone
highlights.body: At $49.50 for 15 days, Stelo removes the two things that used to keep casual users out, a doctor's visit and a monthly membership. It runs the same sensor generation as the Dexcom G7, so the readings you get for spotting how meals and workouts move your glucose are genuinely trustworthy. For a first sensor, nothing else combines this accuracy with this little friction.

highlights.title: Pay for a software platform only when you want coaching
highlights.body: Levels, Nutrisense and Signos all cost three to five times what a bare sensor does, and that premium buys interpretation and coaching, since these platforms run the same sensors you can buy alone. Nutrisense includes a registered dietitian in every plan, Signos holds FDA-cleared weight-management claims, and Levels wraps the data in the cleanest app on the market. If you want a human or an algorithm turning numbers into a plan, they earn it.

highlights.title: Insulin users should still start with the Dexcom G7
highlights.body: The Dexcom G7 keeps its accuracy crown with an 8% MARD, a 30-minute warmup and direct insulin-pump integration. Those three specs matter enormously when your dosing decisions ride on the reading. The FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus is the close runner-up with a 15-day sensor and an 8.2% MARD, and it costs less per day, which is why it is the value pick for daily diabetes management.

highlights.title: January AI proves you can start without a sensor
highlights.body: January AI is the outlier that earns its ranking by needing no hardware at all. Its generative-AI meal scanner predicts your glucose response from a photo, so you can test-drive metabolic awareness for $28 a month before committing to a sensor. As the cheapest door into the category, it earns its spot on the list.

zh-tw.commentary:
連續血糖監測走到 2026，已經變成很多一般人在用的健康工具，這份排行榜就是照這個趨勢排的。我的第一名給 Dexcom Stelo，因為它把最大的入門門檻解決掉了，就是價格跟取得難度。用的是跟 G7 同款的感測器，貼 15 天只要 49.5 美元，免處方、免會員，也沒有硬塞給你的教練方案。對大多數只是好奇一碗滷肉飯或一次晨跑會怎麼影響血糖的人來說，這樣的硬體剛剛好。

第二名 Abbott Lingo 贏在 App。感測器精準度 MARD 大概 9%，拿來做健康管理跟 Stelo 一樣夠用，那個會幫你的飲食、睡眠、運動打分數的教練功能，是我用過對新手最友善的體驗。想要數據附帶一套計畫，Lingo 這個價差花得值得。

醫療級這一段還是 Dexcom G7 跟 FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus 的天下。G7 的 8% MARD、暖機 30 分鐘，到現在還是精準度標竿，能連胰島素幫浦這點，讓打胰島素的人應該先看它。Libre 3 Plus 用 15 天佩戴、8.2% MARD、市面最小的體積回應，每天要管血糖的糖友選它，性價比最高。

軟體平台那三家 Levels、Nutrisense、Signos，就是開始燒錢的地方。Levels 介面最漂亮，Nutrisense 每個方案都配一位真人營養師，Signos 拿了 FDA 認證專攻減重跟 GLP-1 族群。它們的價格是裸感測器的好幾倍，多花的錢買的是數據解讀跟陪跑服務，感測器其實跟你單買的同一批。老實說我只有在你真的想要有人帶著調整的時候才推。Ultrahuman M1 跟 Sibionics GS3 補上生物駭客跟平價兩端，January AI 則靠完全免感測器就能預測血糖，硬是卡進榜單。

highlights.title: 想踏進血糖監測，Stelo 幾乎是所有人的正確起點
highlights.body: 貼 15 天只要 49.5 美元，Stelo 把過去擋住一般人的兩件事拿掉了，一個是要跑一趟診所，一個是每月會員費。它用的是跟 Dexcom G7 同一代的感測器，所以你想看吃一餐、跑一次步血糖會怎麼跳，讀數是真的可以信的。當人生第一片感測器，沒有別的能同時做到這種精準又這麼零負擔。

highlights.title: 軟體平台的錢，想要教練陪你調整再花
highlights.body: Levels、Nutrisense、Signos 的價格是裸感測器的三到五倍，多花的錢買的是數據解讀跟陪跑服務，感測器用的其實跟你單買的同一批。Nutrisense 每個方案都配一位註冊營養師，Signos 拿了 FDA 減重管理認證，Levels 則把數據包進市面上最漂亮的 App。你想要有真人或演算法幫你把數字變成計畫，這錢花得值。

highlights.title: 打胰島素的人，還是從 Dexcom G7 開始
highlights.body: Dexcom G7 靠 8% MARD、暖機 30 分鐘、直接連胰島素幫浦，穩坐精準度王座。當你的用藥劑量要靠讀數決定，這三個規格差一點就差很多。FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus 緊追在後，15 天佩戴、8.2% MARD，每天分攤下來還更便宜，所以每天要管血糖的糖友，它是性價比首選。

highlights.title: January AI 證明免感測器也能先上手
highlights.body: January AI 是榜上的異數，靠的是完全不用任何硬體。它的生成式 AI 餐點掃描能從一張照片預測你的血糖反應，一個月 28 美元就能先試玩代謝管理的感覺，還沒買感測器就能上手。當這個品類最便宜的一道門，它值得榜上這個位置。

en.commentary:
The regulatory news that matters most this summer is the FDA clearing Stelo as the first over-the-counter CGM for children, covering ages two and up for people not using insulin. That is a genuine expansion of what an OTC sensor is permitted to do, and it reinforces why Stelo holds my top spot.

Stelo wins on the intersection of accuracy, wear time and cost. Fifteen days per sensor at a subscription price well under the prescription options gives it the best daily cost in this ranking by a clear margin, and its accuracy is close enough to the G7 that the gap does not change decisions for a non-insulin user. That is the honest framing: buy accuracy you can afford to wear continuously.

The Dexcom G7 15 Day at second remains the accuracy leader with the strongest MARD figures available to consumers, and it is the correct choice for anyone dosing insulin. Precision matters differently when a reading drives a therapeutic decision.

Abbott's Lingo at third has the best app experience here. Its glucose-spike scoring translates raw data into something actionable for someone with no clinical training, which is genuinely the hardest part of consumer CGM. Eversense 365 deserves its own mention for a one-year implanted sensor, which is a fundamentally different ownership model from a sensor you replace every two weeks.

highlights.title: OTC clearance for children is the meaningful regulatory move this year
highlights.body: The FDA cleared the Stelo Glucose Biosensor System as the first over-the-counter CGM for children aged two and up who do not use insulin. That expands the addressable population for prescription-free continuous monitoring substantially. Regulatory reach is a real ranking factor in this category, because it determines who can actually buy the sensor without a clinical gatekeeper.

highlights.title: Buy the accuracy you can afford to wear every day
highlights.body: Stelo runs 15 days per sensor at a subscription cost well below the prescription options, giving it the best daily cost in this ranking. Its accuracy sits close enough to the G7 that the difference does not change decisions for someone not dosing insulin. A sensor you wear continuously for a year teaches you more than a more accurate one you stop buying after three months.

highlights.title: If you dose insulin, accuracy stops being a tradeoff
highlights.body: The Dexcom G7 15 Day carries the strongest MARD figures available to consumers, and when a glucose reading drives an insulin decision, that precision is not a nice-to-have. This is the one use case where I would tell someone to ignore the daily cost column entirely and buy on accuracy alone. Its 15-day wear also cuts the annual sensor count meaningfully.

highlights.title: The app is where consumer CGM actually succeeds or fails
highlights.body: Abbott's Lingo scores glucose spikes and translates raw curves into guidance someone with no clinical training can act on. Handing an untrained user a stream of interstitial glucose numbers produces confusion rather than behavior change. Lingo does the interpretation work, and that is the single hardest problem in this category, which is why it holds third despite mid-pack sensor specifications.

zh-tw.commentary:
今年夏天最重要的法規消息，是 FDA 通過 Stelo 成為第一款可用於兒童的非處方連續血糖監測，涵蓋兩歲以上、未使用胰島素的族群。這是 OTC 感測器被允許做的事情的實質擴張，也強化了 Stelo 為什麼站在我的第一名。

Stelo 贏在準確度、配戴天數跟成本的交集。一片十五天，訂閱價遠低於處方選項，讓它的每日成本在這份榜單裡領先一大截，而它的準確度跟 G7 已經接近到，對不打胰島素的使用者來說那個差距不會改變任何決定。這是誠實的講法：買你負擔得起長期戴著的準確度。

第二名的 Dexcom G7 15 Day 依然是準確度王者，MARD 數字是消費者能拿到最好的，打胰島素的人就該選它。當一個讀數會直接驅動治療決策時，精準度的意義完全不同。

第三名 Abbott Lingo 的 App 體驗是這裡最好的。它的血糖波動評分把原始數據翻譯成沒有臨床訓練的人也能行動的東西，而這其實是消費級 CGM 最難的部分。Eversense 365 值得單獨一提，植入式感測器可以用一年，這跟每兩週換一次的擁有模式根本是不同的東西。

highlights.title: 今年真正重要的法規動作，是兒童 OTC 適應症通過
highlights.body: FDA 通過 Stelo 血糖生物感測系統成為第一款可供兩歲以上、未使用胰島素兒童使用的非處方 CGM。這讓免處方連續監測的可觸及人口大幅擴張。法規涵蓋範圍在這個品類是實質的排名因素，因為它決定了誰能真的在沒有臨床守門人的情況下買到感測器。

highlights.title: 買你負擔得起天天戴的那個準確度
highlights.body: Stelo 一片十五天，訂閱成本遠低於處方選項，每日成本是這份榜單裡最好的。它的準確度跟 G7 已經接近到，對不打胰島素的人來說那個差異不會改變任何決定。一個你連續戴一年的感測器，教你的東西會比一個更準但你三個月後就不買的多得多。

highlights.title: 要打胰島素的話，準確度就不再是取捨項目
highlights.body: Dexcom G7 15 Day 的 MARD 數字是消費者能取得最強的，而當血糖讀數直接決定胰島素劑量時，這個精準度不是加分項而是必需品。這是唯一一個我會叫人完全忽略每日成本欄、單看準確度來買的使用情境。十五天的配戴時間也讓一年要用的感測器數量明顯下降。

highlights.title: 消費級 CGM 的成敗，其實在 App
highlights.body: Abbott Lingo 會為血糖波動評分，把原始曲線翻譯成沒有臨床訓練的人也能照著做的建議。直接丟一串組織液血糖數字給沒受訓的使用者，得到的是困惑而不是行為改變。Lingo 幫你把解讀這一段做掉，而這是這個品類最難的問題，所以它感測器規格中段卻能站第三。

en.commentary: Dexcom Stelo keeps first place because it made continuous glucose monitoring accessible without a prescription while retaining Dexcom's sensor accuracy, and access is what determines whether this technology reaches the people who benefit from it. For someone with prediabetes or general metabolic curiosity, Stelo removes both the gatekeeping and a large part of the cost barrier. The G7 15 Day sits second and represents the more important engineering achievement in this category. Extending wear time from ten to fifteen days cuts the annual sensor count by a third, and since sensor cost is the dominant expense in long term CGM use, that change does more for affordability than any price promotion. Abbott Lingo holds third and remains the better app experience for people who want coaching rather than raw numbers. The standard G7 keeps fourth as the clinical reference for anyone managing diagnosed diabetes with insulin dosing, where proven accuracy and integration with pumps matter above all. FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus takes fifth. My August advice is to plan for the adhesive rather than the sensor. Summer heat and swimming are the two things that end a wear cycle early, and a box of overpatches costs a fraction of a replacement sensor. Apply the patch on day one rather than on the day it starts lifting.

highlights.title: Fifteen day wear is the real cost breakthrough
highlights.body: Extending from ten to fifteen days cuts annual sensor count by a third. Since sensors dominate the long term cost of CGM use, that engineering change does more for affordability than any promotional pricing, which is why the G7 15 Day sits second.

highlights.title: Stelo wins on access, and access is the point
highlights.body: Removing the prescription requirement while keeping Dexcom sensor accuracy brings this technology to people with prediabetes and general metabolic interest. Reaching those users matters more than a marginal accuracy edge, which is why it holds first.

highlights.title: Insulin users should stay with the standard G7
highlights.body: Managing diagnosed diabetes with insulin dosing demands proven accuracy and pump integration above all else. That requirement is specific enough to override the ranking order, and the clinical G7 remains the correct choice for it.

highlights.title: Buy overpatches and apply them on day one
highlights.body: Summer heat and swimming end more wear cycles than sensor failure does. A box of overpatches costs a fraction of one replacement sensor, and applying on day one works far better than reacting when an edge starts lifting.

zh-tw.commentary:
Dexcom Stelo 守住第一，因為它讓連續血糖監測不用處方就能買到，同時保住 Dexcom 的感測器準確度，而可及性正是決定這個技術能不能真的碰到需要的人的關鍵。對糖尿病前期或者只是想搞懂自己代謝狀況的人來說，Stelo 同時拿掉了門檻跟一大半的成本障礙。

Dexcom G7 15 Day 排第二，我認為它才是這個品類更重要的工程成就。配戴天數從十天拉到十五天，一年要用的感測器數量直接少三分之一，而感測器成本本來就是長期使用 CGM 的最大開銷，這個改變對可負擔性的貢獻，大過任何促銷價。

Abbott Lingo 第三，想要的是引導而不是原始數字的人，它的 App 體驗比較好。標準版 G7 守在第四，是確診糖尿病、要靠數據調胰島素劑量的人的臨床參考，這種情境下準確度跟幫浦整合壓過一切。FreeStyle Libre 3 Plus 第五。

八月的建議是，預算要留給貼片，不是感測器。台灣夏天這個濕熱加上游泳，是提早中斷配戴週期的兩大殺手，而一盒防水加強貼的錢只佔一片感測器的一小部分。第一天就貼上去，不要等到邊緣翹起來那天才處理。

en.commentary: Two things happened in this category this month that a buyer needs to know, and only one of them affects the ranking. The first is Dexcom's public warning that certain G7 sensor lots which were designated for destruction were stolen during the scrap process and resold through third-party sellers. That is a supply chain integrity problem, and my practical advice is direct: buy G7 and Stelo sensors from the pharmacy counter, Dexcom directly, or a named retail account, and check the lot number against Dexcom's notice before you apply one. A sensor that sat in an uncontrolled environment can read accurately for a day and then drift, which is the worst possible failure mode for something you dose or eat by. This does not change my scores, because the devices themselves are unaffected, and it should not push anyone off a platform that works for them. The second development is Abbott's CE Mark for Libre Duo, a dual glucose and ketone sensor measuring both every minute. Ketone visibility matters most for anyone on an insulin pump or a GLP-1, where rising ketones are the early signal of a problem that a glucose curve alone will show too late. That is a European clearance today, so it stays off this board until a US pathway is visible, but it tells you where Abbott is taking the platform. Stelo holds first at 9.3 because it remains the cheapest legitimate entry into continuous data with no prescription, 15 day wear, and readings every 15 minutes. Dexcom G7 15 Day stays second at 9.1 for anyone who needs one minute granularity and pump integration. Abbott Lingo third at 9.0. No changes to ranks or scores today.

en.commentary:
The market has now split cleanly in two, and understanding which half you are shopping in settles most of the confusion in this category. Prescription grade CGMs built for diabetes management sit on one side, and over the counter wellness sensors aimed at metabolic curiosity sit on the other. You can buy the second kind off a shelf at Walmart with no prescription at all.

The safety line between them is firm and worth stating plainly. OTC sensors are not cleared for insulin dosing. If you take insulin, the device you need is a prescription iCGM, and that is a conversation with your clinician rather than a shopping decision.

On accuracy, the current figures are close enough to be interesting. Dexcom Stelo runs around 10 percent MARD and Abbott Lingo around 9.3 percent, which is the gap behind Lingo's 9.0 accuracy score against Stelo's 9.2 overall composite. Stelo holds first at 9.3 because its daily cost score of 9.5 is the highest here by a clear margin, and for a sensor you wear continuously, cost per day is the factor that determines whether you are still wearing it in month three.

Dexcom G7 15 Day holds second at 9.1 with the best accuracy on the board at 9.8, which is what a longer wear window plus a mature algorithm buys. Abbott Lingo stays third at 9.0 with a 9.2 app score, and both Stelo and Lingo now feed Apple Health along with third party tools, so the data does not stay locked in one vendor's app. No rank or score changes today.

highlights.title: OTC sensors are not cleared for insulin dosing
highlights.body: Over the counter CGMs including Stelo and Lingo are cleared as wellness and general health tools. Anyone dosing insulin needs a prescription iCGM, and that decision belongs with a clinician rather than being settled at a pharmacy shelf.

highlights.title: MARD is the accuracy number, and the field is tight
highlights.body: Dexcom Stelo runs around 10 percent MARD and Abbott Lingo around 9.3 percent, which is close enough that other factors decide the purchase. The Dexcom G7 15 Day leads this board at 9.8 for accuracy, earned through a longer wear window and a mature algorithm.

highlights.title: Cost per day is what determines whether you keep wearing it
highlights.body: Stelo holds first at 9.3 on a daily cost score of 9.5, the highest here by a clear margin. A sensor only produces useful data while it is on your arm, so the recurring cost matters more over six months than any single specification.

highlights.title: Check the integrations before you commit to a platform
highlights.body: Stelo and Lingo both feed Apple Health and third party apps including SNAQ, with Stelo also connecting to Oura. Data that flows into tools you already use is what turns a two week experiment into a habit worth keeping.

en.commentary:
The Dexcom Stelo stays at number one for the audience this list actually serves. Most people reading a consumer CGM ranking do not have diabetes and are trying to understand how their own meals affect them. Stelo is built for exactly that, sold without a prescription, and priced so a two sensor month is a decision you can make without insurance involvement.

The G7 15 Day holds second and is the better instrument. Longer wear reduces the number of insertions per year, the accuracy is clinical grade, and for anyone managing diabetes with a physician that is the correct choice.

Abbott's Lingo sits third with the friendliest coaching layer. If your interest is behavioral rather than clinical, the app does more to turn a glucose curve into a decision about what to eat tomorrow.

My practical advice for anyone starting this month: run your first sensor without changing anything about your diet. The instinct is to eat carefully while wearing it, and that produces a clean chart that teaches you nothing. Eat normally for the first two weeks, find the three meals that spike hardest, and then experiment on those specific meals with the second sensor. That method produces changes you will keep.
